obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (SSN with name is covered in every state; bank account numbers, driver license numbers, and other elements vary)
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
notify: Affected residents of each state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected associates and candidates reside; counsel's state matrix
clock_starts: Varies by state (often determination of a breach)
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with outside counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state requires

trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the firm (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains the firm's personal information has a breach
deadline: Varies by state; firm contracts require 72 hours for tier-1 vendors
notify: The firm (SOC and Director of Third-Party Risk Management)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (name with SSN, driver license or passport number, a financial account number with a code or password that permits access, or geolocation, among other listed elements)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days if good cause for delay is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within the 30 days
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 140,000 current and former associates with Florida addresses in the payroll engine
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, content of notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the firm reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports the determination; not available when SSNs were exported

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request (may be extended or revoked in writing)
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the firm (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent (payroll, ATS, onboarding, time capture, screening, paycard vendors)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The firm
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors holding Florida residents' personal information

citation: E-Verify MOU for Employers Art. II.A.16
trigger: Suspected or confirmed loss of control of, or unauthorized access to, E-Verify personal data (case data and results stored with Forms I-9 in SYS-02, or E-Verify credentials)
deadline: Immediately
notify: DHS E-Verify by phone (888-464-4218) or email (E-Verify@dhs.gov) with the subject 'Privacy Incident - Password'
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SYS-02 records or an E-Verify account is involved

obligation: IRS notice of Form W-2 data loss (guidance)
citation: IRS guidance: Form W-2/SSN data theft information for businesses and payroll service providers
trigger: Theft of employee W-2 or SSN data
deadline: As soon as possible (the IRS may be able to protect employees from tax-related identity theft if told quickly)
notify: IRS at dataloss@irs.gov with the subject 'W2 Data Loss' and a contact; do not attach employee personal information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but recommended; the payroll engine holds W-2 and SSN data for associates
clock_starts: Confirmation of W-2 or SSN data theft

trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.4)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, incident responders with knowledge, and executives (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

trigger: Incident affecting federal contract information or contract performance
deadline: Per each contract's clause; FAR 52.204-21 itself sets no reporting clock
notify: Contracting officers for affected contracts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Government Solutions data (agency timesheets, invoices, rosters) is involved; check each of the 34 contracts

obligation: Covered telecommunications, Kaspersky, or FASCSA article discovered
trigger: Covered equipment, service, or article found in use (for example, during forensic review)
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)) or a FASCSA covered article (52.204-30); further report within 10 business days in each case
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for contracts that include the clauses; only if such an article is found

obligation: SL-1 Workforce Management Platform client notice
trigger: Security incident affecting SL-1 client data or service
deadline: Per agreement (standard term: 72 hours for a security incident; 4 hours for a Severity-1 outage)
notify: About 60 managed-program clients
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if WMP data or service is affected (not in the base scenario)
owner: Vice President, Product, Workforce Management Platform

trigger: Incident affecting client-sourced workers' data or pay
deadline: Per agreement (standard term: 72 hours)
notify: About 340 payrolling clients
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SL-2 workers are in the payroll engine

obligation: Hospital client notice under contractual BAAs
trigger: Incident affecting information the firm holds under a hospital agreement (clinician schedules, hospital contacts); HIPAA 164.410 does not apply because the firm is not a business associate
deadline: Per agreement (most say 5 business days)
notify: 37 hospital clients with BAAs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if hospital information is involved; check each agreement
owner: President, Healthcare Staffing with the Chief Privacy Officer

trigger: Incident affecting client information (client contacts, timesheets, bill rates)
deadline: Per contract (large clients commonly require 72 hours)
notify: Client security contacts in the contract register
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if client data is involved; associate-only data triggers few contracts

obligation: Originating banks and paycard program manager
citation: Cash management and paycard program agreements (contract)
trigger: Diverted ACH credits or paycard loads, or compromise of file transfer credentials
deadline: Immediately on discovery; ask the banks to attempt recall of fraudulent entries (recall success and timing depend on the receiving bank and network rules, not verified here)
notify: Banks A and B; paycard program manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - bank changes are part of the scenario

trigger: Suspected security incident or fraudulent funds transfer
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging vendors
notify: Carrier
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: Payroll diversion, data theft, or extortion
deadline: As early as practical (supports fund recovery, OFAC mitigation, and any law enforcement delay request)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any extortion or ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until it takes effect

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held for a covered entity
deadline: No later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: HIPAA covered entity client
applies_at_this_tier: No - the firm is not a business associate (P03 G-180); hospital BAAs are handled as contracts (row above)
